problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,3]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}xy-1 \\ {y}^{3}-{x}^{2}y+2\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[1,\,1]^{T}.$

| ${x}_{1}=[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $0.5$ |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}-{x}^{2}y+2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}-{x}^{2}y+2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ -2xy & 3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ -2xy & 3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}x & y \\ -2xy & 3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ -2xy & 3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}xy-1 \\ {y}^{3}-{x}^{2}y+2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2(1)(1) & 3(1)^{2}-(1)^{2}\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(1)(1)-1 \\ (1)^{3}-(1)^{2}(1)+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-1\cdot (-2)}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.5 \\ 0.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
